title: Clifft: Fast Exact Simulation of Near-Clifford Quantum Circuits
conversion_notes: The coherent surface-code workloads already contain R_Z rotations in extended Stim syntax; no T conversion is needed. The companion paper states it provides exact circuit files and generation scripts. Cultivation workloads also contain real T gates.
notes: The paper benchmarks rotated memory-Z at (distance, rounds) (3,1), (3,3), (5,1), (5,5); the coherent variants use R_Z(0.02) at depolarization sites. R_Z is non-Clifford but the prescribed status vocabulary has no native-rotation option. Standard Stim cannot parse the extension. Paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27058 ; check rotation angle conventions across simulators. Note SymFT README describes replacement of depolarization, whereas Clifft paper text says co-located; inspect the precise chosen file.

title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
conversion_notes: The coherent_surface_* files already contain R_Z(0.02), so no conversion is needed; these are extended Stim syntax, not parseable by ordinary Stim. README specifies angles in half turns: 0.02 means 0.02*pi radians. Check Tsim's convention before running.
notes: Four coherent rotated surface-code inputs at d/r 3/1, 3/3, 5/1, 5/5. README says generated DEPOLARIZE1 and DEPOLARIZE2 are replaced by R_Z on the same targets, while reset and measurement errors remain stochastic. Files are checked in, with no regeneration script; Clifft-derived so overlapping rather than independent workloads. Native R_Z has no corresponding option in the requested status vocabulary.

title: Modular Neural Decoder for Surface Code Memory and Logic on Superconducting Processors
conversion_notes: Use the released d=3 X-type stability circuit and insert R_X(alpha) on every measure qubit immediately before each readout, as specified by the paper; check angle units. The released simulations use stochastic models, while the coherent sweep was performed on IBM hardware.
notes: Repository documents Stim simulation generator and noiseless stability/ZZ-merge circuit files; Zenodo contains measured detector events for the coherent-angle sweep, not claimed to contain extended Stim circuits. Confirm exact file syntax and whether the circuit faithfully captures the hardware no-reset schedule before claiming reproduction. Paper section IV.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.03869

title: SOFT: a high-performance simulator for universal fault-tolerant quantum circuits
authors: Li, Zheng, Zhang, Lou, Ying, Liu, Sun
conversion_notes: The paper directly simulates d=5 cultivation with 72 T/T-dagger gates; inspect the legacy circuit files for the input dialect and whether translation to extended Stim is required. Current benchmark directory provides related extended Stim T-gate circuits.
notes: The original paper explicitly cites the public SOFT repository for reproducing its results. This is a near-Clifford simulator/cultivation candidate, not a coherent-overrotation experiment; the present benchmark corpus is a later SymFT revision, so do not assume all benchmark files are exactly those of the 2025 paper. https://arxiv.org/html/2512.23037

title: Coherent errors and readout errors in the surface code
conversion_notes: Reconstruct the physical surface-code stabilizer measurements and Z rotations as a Stim-style circuit from the described phenomenological model; add measurement readout flips. This is not established as a ready-to-run Stim generator and reconstruction is substantive.
notes: The authors explicitly release the Python Majorana/FLO simulation used for the paper, but it does not appear to supply Stim circuits; included as a reconstructable lead, not as a verified Stim match. Phenomenological repeated measurements rather than a circuit-level gate-noise model. Paper reference: https://quantum-journal.org/papers/q-2023-09-21-1116/pdf/
